claim: Devala deliberately constructs a sand stupa, adorns it, and venerates Buddhas through it.
allowed_wording: The account illustrates intentional commemorative devotion and the beneficial results the text associates with it.
prohibited_overclaim: Do not call it an early discourse or claim that it formally defines every sand stupa as Uddesika Cetiya.

claim: Nārada deliberately constructs and venerates a sand stupa for Buddhas.
allowed_wording: Use the stable text identifier and note that edition numbering may differ.
prohibited_overclaim: Do not copy an uncertain secondary rendering or claim a formal Uddesika definition.

claim: Later Theravāda explanation distinguishes bodily-relic, use-associated, and memorial or representational shrines.
allowed_wording: Present the threefold framework as later Theravāda narrative or commentary.
prohibited_overclaim: Do not present the prose as a verbatim early-discourse definition shared identically by all Buddhist schools.

claim: The sand-stupa stories help illustrate a broader logic of commemorative or representational devotion.
source: Editorial comparison of the two Apadāna accounts with Ja 479
allowed_wording: Label the connection as an interpretive comparison informed by Theravāda memorial traditions.
prohibited_overclaim: Do not say the Apadāna explicitly classifies every sand stupa as Uddesika Cetiya.

claim: Intention matters but does not automatically make any random object a cetiya.
allowed_wording: Require deliberate dedication or representational function in the explanation.
prohibited_overclaim: Do not claim emotion magically transforms any object into a cetiya.

claim: Devotees wanted a focus for offerings while the Buddha was absent; Anāthapiṇḍika raised the issue; Ānanda asked about shrines and proposed a Bodhi tree; the proposal was approved and the tree planted.
allowed_wording: Paraphrase the verified narrative sequence and identify its later textual layer.
prohibited_overclaim: Do not present the prose as an early-discourse transcript.

claim: Ja 479 records neither a statue proposal nor a rejection of Buddha images.
allowed_wording: State only what the narrative records and does not record.
prohibited_overclaim: Do not put a hypothetical approval of a statue into the Buddha's mouth.

claim: A surviving seated Gandhāran Buddha is dated to the first to mid-second century CE.
source: Seated Buddha from Gandhāra, Metropolitan Museum of Art, accession 1987.218.1
allowed_wording: Use as limited chronology for securely attested human-form imagery.
prohibited_overclaim: Do not infer a universal earlier image prohibition or Ānanda's undocumented motive.

claim: Human-form Buddha traditions developed in Gandhāra and contemporaneously in Mathurā.
source: Buddhism and Buddhist Art, Metropolitan Museum of Art
prohibited_overclaim: Do not project a fully developed later image culture into the narrative setting.

claim: Silence about a statue is not by itself a prohibition against later Buddha images.
source: Echo Buddha inference bounded by Ja 479
allowed_wording: Frame as a logical limit on arguments from silence.
prohibited_overclaim: Do not claim the text affirmatively authorizes every later image practice.
